claims.claim_text: GPTZero's Hallucination Detector automatically identifies hallucinated sources and poorly supported claims in essays to help educators verify academic integrity.
claims.evidence_span: GPTZero's Hallucination Detector automatically detects hallucinated sources and poorly supported claims in essays.

claims.claim_text: The source finder tool detects checkable, objective claims in text and matches them to online, academic, and publicly available data sources.
claims.evidence_span: Source finder will detect as many checkable, objective claims in your text and match those to sources from online, academic, and publicly available data coming from AI-powered search engines.

claims.claim_text: An AI hallucination is defined as a generated response containing false or misleading information presented as fact.
claims.evidence_span: In the field of artificial intelligence (AI), a hallucination or artificial hallucination (also called bullshitting, confabulation, delusion, or mirage) is a response generated by AI that contains false or misleading information presented as fact.

claims.claim_text: Symbolic artificial intelligence models generally do not produce hallucinations, unlike large language models.
claims.evidence_span: Symbolic artificial intelligence models generally do not produce hallucinations, unlike large language models.

claims.claim_text: The survey paper provides an extensive overview of current techniques employed to detect, verify, mitigate, or correct hallucinations in generative AI models.
claims.evidence_span: The present survey aims to provide an extensive overview of current techniques employed to detect, verify, mitigate, or correct hallucinations in generative AI models.

claims.claim_text: The survey analyzes enabling technologies such as transformer-based language models, dense retrieval systems, knowledge graphs, and truth-scoring frameworks.
claims.evidence_span: In addition, enabling technologies such as transformer-based language models, dense retrieval systems, knowledge graphs, credibility assessment mechanisms, and truth-scoring frameworks are analyzed from the perspective of reliable content verification.

claims.claim_text: AI hallucinations are instances where an AI system produces outputs that sound plausible but are factually wrong, irrelevant, or entirely fabricated.
claims.evidence_span: AI hallucinations are instances where an AI system produces outputs that sound plausible but are factually wrong, irrelevant or entirely fabricated.

claims.claim_text: Contextual hallucinations occur when an AI relies on its general training data instead of requested contextual data like a specific document or database.
claims.evidence_span: Contextual hallucinations happen when the AI is supposed to answer a prompt by using specific contextual data, such as a document or database, but instead relies on its general training data.

claims.claim_text: An AI hallucination occurs when a language model produces content that sounds authoritative and well-reasoned but is factually wrong or entirely made up.
claims.evidence_span: An AI hallucination is when a language model produces content that sounds authoritative and well-reasoned but is factually wrong or entirely made up.

claims.claim_text: Combining Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback, and guardrails can lead to a 96% reduction in hallucinations.
claims.evidence_span: A 2024 Stanford study found that combining Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF), and guardrails led to a 96% reduction in hallucinations.
